assignment_name: Module One Assignment 1 - Forecast and EDA
label_note:
eda_01 is a real submission to this assignment, read step by step against the nine criteria; every step is done and explained, so it is labelled full marks. The rest are derived from it mechanically (scripts/make_eda_variants.py) so that exactly one thing separates each from full marks. A rubric with only 1/0 levels means satisfies must be 1 or 0 -- there is no half credit to award.

THE JUDGMENT WORTH ARGUING WITH: eda_02 has correct code for Steps 3 and 6 that was never executed, and both are labelled 0. Nothing was verified, nothing was removed, no plot exists, and the assignment's own submission requirements demand code that 'runs successfully for all the questions'. A course that credits correct-but-unrun code should change these labels rather than the grader -- and then the measurement means something different.

WHY eda_03 AND eda_05 ARE BOTH HERE: they are the same damage -- one call misspelled, one traceback -- with opposite correct answers, and the first version of this label set got the second one wrong. Step 6 asks for a heatmap, so when the heatmap call raises there is no heatmap and the step is not done: eda_03 loses those 2 points. Step 3 asks to verify duplicates and eliminate them ONLY IF any are identified; this dataset has none, which the student's own duplicated().sum() output shows as np.int64(0), so the call that crashed was a no-op and the step is complete: eda_05 keeps all 14. A grader that deducts on eda_05 is reacting to the traceback instead of reading the criterion, and that is a failure worth catching.
